name: Proreta
line: Your texts, email, and calendar, in one private workspace.
description: Proreta brings your texts, email, and calendar together around each person. A private prototype, being built for open-source, self-hosted use.
headline: Keep up with the people in your life.
about: Proreta brings texts, email, and calendar context together around each person, helping you remember details, track commitments, and prepare replies.
delivery: Being built for open-source, self-hosted use, with AI-guided installation.

blocks.heading: Setup
blocks.title: Guided installation, step by step
blocks.intro: Proreta is meant to be installed with an AI assistant at your side. It explains each step in plain words, runs the checks, and helps when one doesn't pass. The prototype is installed this way today, one stage at a time; the public installer is planned.

items.title: Check your setup
items.text: A first check says whether your computers and accounts meet the requirements below, before anything is installed.

items.title: Install, and choose privacy settings
items.text: Each part installs on its own computer. Along the way you choose how strict to be, such as which people never leave your own computers.

items.title: Connect accounts and approve access
items.text: Give Gmail and Google Calendar read-only access, let the Mac helper read Messages, and register your YubiKey.

items.title: Check it works, then meet your people
items.text: Built-in checks confirm that every part is reading, nothing was marked as read, and nothing was sent. Then a guided session walks you through the people you message most.

blocks.heading: Requirements
blocks.intro: What the prototype runs on today. The public release's requirements aren't settled yet.

items.title: A Mac at home
items.text: iMessage and SMS can only be read on a Mac signed in to your Apple account, so one has to stay on at home. The prototype uses a Mac mini.

items.title: A security key
items.text: Opening Proreta, and every step that loosens privacy, needs a touch of a security key such as a YubiKey. Two are best, one as a spare.

items.title: A computer for the local AI model
items.text: Sorting, the briefing, and drafts run on an AI model at home. The prototype uses a mini PC with 128 GB of memory, shared with its graphics.

items.title: An always-on home server
items.text: Stores everything and serves Proreta's page. The prototype uses a Synology NAS, beside a small mini PC that reads mail and calendars.

items.title: Accounts it reads
items.text: Messages on your Mac, and Gmail with read-only access; Google Calendar, also read-only, is being added. Other email and calendar services aren't supported yet.

items.title: Where you use it
items.text: In a browser on your own computers, on your home network. Use away from home and a phone version are planned.

items.title: A VPN
items.text: Only needed to reach your home computers from elsewhere, for example to install an update while traveling. Proreta itself has no public address.

items.title: A separate network
items.text: Recommended, not required: Proreta's computers on their own walled-off part of your home network. The prototype runs this way.

items.title: Updates
items.text: Each update checks itself before and after it installs, and keeps a way back to the version before.

items.title: Backups
items.text: A snapshot of Proreta's data is taken before every update and kept until the next one passes. Regular backups of your server stay up to you.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text: A status line names anything late: a reader that stopped, a disk filling up, or a certificate near its end. Each install's checks print plain PASS or FAIL lines that an AI assistant can walk through with you.

items.title: Removing it
items.text: Removing Proreta's access in your Google account stops all reading of mail and calendars at once. What it kept stays in its folders on your own computers, for you to keep or delete.

blocks.heading: Privacy and data flows
blocks.title: What Proreta reads stays on your computers at home.
blocks.intro: A cloud AI is optional. It ships switched off, and you decide, person by person, what it may read.

items.title: Your computers at home
items: A local AI model sorts, summarizes, and drafts
Money and health messages never leave

blocks.heading: How the limits are enforced

items.title: Not publicly accessible
items.text: Proreta has no public address. Its page answers only your own computers on your home network, always over HTTPS with certificates made at home, and only after a touch of your YubiKey.

items.title: Read-only access
items.text: It reads Gmail, and soon Google Calendar, with Google's read-only permissions, so it can't send, change, or delete mail or events. Unread messages stay unread.

items.title: Money and health stay home
items.text: As each message arrives, your own computers check it against fixed lists of money and health words. A match, or a maybe, marks it, and a mark is only ever added, never taken off. The rule that decides what may go to a cloud AI refuses anything marked, and it runs where your messages are stored, not in the page.

items.title: The cloud AI connection
items.text: It ships shut, and only you can open it, at your home server: no page or script can. Once it's open, everything that leaves is logged word for word, and the words are kept for 30 days. The prototype's cloud AI is Claude, from Anthropic.

items.title: What a cloud AI may receive
items.text: Messages with people you've cleared one by one with your YubiKey, with phone numbers, email addresses, and street addresses swapped for stand-ins. A message with a number of four or more digits, or one of your code words, is never sent. In the current design, email, group chats, calls, photos, and anything marked stay home.

items.title: A touch of your key
items.text: Opening Proreta, clearing a person for the cloud AI, and later sending a message each need a touch of your YubiKey, checked where your messages are stored.

items.title: An emergency stop
items.text: Texting STOP pauses everything at once.

items.title: A walled-off network
items.text: In the prototype, Proreta's computers sit on their own walled-off part of the home network. The software doesn't need this; the guide will recommend it.

blocks.note: When the source is published, each of these points will link to the code and documentation behind it. Published code lets you check how Proreta works; it doesn't prove every claim by itself.
blocks.intro: Each of these is built into the software, except the last, which is how the prototype is set up.

blocks.heading: Where it stands

items.title: Today
items.text: A private prototype has run at the developer's home since November 2026, for the developer's own accounts: texts and email by person, circles, the Watch, Remind, and Draft setting, cloud AI access set person by person, and sign-in with a YubiKey.

items.title: Next
items.text: Calendar plans and who's waiting, the morning briefing, notes and facts, calls, and replies drafted at home. Each part is tested on made-up data before it's installed.

items.title: Later
items.text: Opening the cloud AI for people you've cleared, sending from Proreta, reminders, search, WhatsApp and Messenger, a phone version, and the public installer.

items.title: Source code
items.text: To be published as open source with the public release.

privacy.intro: This policy covers Proreta, a private command center that reads its owner's own messages, email and calendar. Only its owner signs in to it, with the owner's own accounts.
collects: Email: with the read-only Gmail access that the owner grants at Google's sign-in, it reads the messages in the owner's own Gmail accounts, with their headers and labels.
Calendar: with read-only Google Calendar access granted the same way, it reads the events on the owner's own calendars, such as their times, titles, places and guests.
Texts and contacts: on the owner's own computers, it reads the owner's own text messages and contacts.
It can't send, change or delete mail or calendar events, and it reads nothing else in the Google account.
privacy.uses: Only to help the owner keep up with the owner's own messages, email and calendar, for example by showing them in one place, sorting them and noting what needs an answer.
privacy.shares: It's never sold, used for ads or used to train AI models. What it reads is kept on the owner's own devices. The owner may let an AI assistant read some of it, only to help with the owner's own messages.
privacy.keeps: For as long as the owner keeps it on those devices. Removing Proreta's access in the Google account stops all further reading of email and calendar.
privacy.choices: The owner can remove its access at any time, under [Third-party apps and services](https://myaccount.google.com/connections) in the Google account.

extra.heading: Google user data
paragraphs: Proreta's use and transfer of information received from Google APIs adheres to the [Google API Services User Data Policy](https://developers.google.com/terms/api-services-user-data-policy), including the Limited Use requirements.
Proreta is a private tool for its owner's own use. It isn't offered, sold or licensed to anyone else, and no one else may sign in to it.
